name: opendss_altdss_library

support_targets.opendss: EPRI OpenDSS; online documentation is mixed-version

validation.source_review: Line/LineCode, Phase 3A and Phase 3B packages 1 through 6 passed independent QA/QC and architect review and are accepted. Phase 4 package 4.1 (fixture harness and snapshot goldens) passed coder validation, independent QA/QC (PASS, no required corrections) and the architect review (PASS WITH FINDINGS: E-1 per-element loss semantics clarified in the Phase 4 design, O-1 to O-4 recorded) and is accepted by the owner (decision 16), which freezes the fixture pin and both revision 1 goldens as fixed reference data. Fixture inputs are byte-identical to electricdss-tst @ 3b20839 in both the working tree and the repository blobs, and both revision 1 goldens reproduce on the pinned stack. Phase 4 package 4.2 (RegControl catalog) passed coder validation, independent QA/QC (PASS, no required corrections) and the architect review (PASS WITH FINDINGS: F-1 asks for one clause on PTPhase out-of-range readback, A-1 corrected the handoff's #123 claim, O-1 to O-4 recorded) and is accepted by the owner (decision 18), with its one finding carried as a rider on package 4.3. Phase 4 package 4.3 (LoadShape catalog and the ieee13 daily profile) passed coder validation, independent QA/QC (PASS, no required corrections) and the architect review (PASS WITH FINDINGS: A-1 and A-2 corrected architect documents, O-1 to O-3 recorded) and is accepted by the owner (decision 19), which freezes the daily golden at revision 1; the snapshot goldens are unchanged by hash. Phase 4 package 4.4 (cross-interface comparison) passed coder validation, independent QA/QC (PASS, no required corrections) and the architect review (PASS, no required corrections; O-1 to O-4 recorded) and is accepted by the owner (decision 20), with the four observations carried into package 4.5. Phase 4 package 4.5 (exit) passed coder validation, independent QA/QC (PASS, no required corrections) and the architect review (PASS WITH FINDINGS: R-1 restores the checksum and class-coverage gates that the exit checklist dropped from the design's own list, R-2 records the QA/QC outcome in checklist row 5; O-1 to O-4 recorded) and awaits the corrections plus owner acceptance. That review re-observed all 16 troubleshooting records and reproduced the 18/18 pairs, 19 examples, three fixture runs and the byte-identical comparison report; it also corrected three architect documents (the `tested` field's reachability, the `TapNumber` setter, and the capacitor `States` length). Both findings are now closed. That earlier review reproduced the committed report byte-identically in 6.9 s, confirmed 19 examples, 18/18 schema pairs and three fixture runs, hashed all three goldens unchanged at the baseline blob, the current blob and the working tree, and seeded five changes to prove the comparison guards fail when they should. Phase 5: package 5.1 (thin object index) is accepted by the owner (decision 23) after an architect review that re-derived every count in the file from the file it points at; package 5.2 (retrieval tool) is accepted by the owner (decision 24) after a review that ran every canonical query and corrupted three index fields in a scratch copy to prove `--check` exits 1 and names them, with the one gap that a corrupted `fixture_usage` entry is caught by the schema rather than by `--check` recorded as an observation; and package 5.3 (release record) is issued under charter step 7. Package 5.3 (release record) passed coder validation, independent QA/QC (PASS, no required corrections) and the architect review (PASS WITH FINDINGS: R-1, the alias registry missing from the retrieval workflow and the package README inventory; F-2, the `Official-current` row needing its corpus scope stated) and is accepted by the owner (decision 25) at release v1.0.0, which promotes schema_version to 1.0.0 and tags this commit. The review re-derived every published count from the catalogs and corrupted the alias registry eight ways to prove `--check` fails and names the alias. Both findings were remediated, re-QA'd and verified by re-running the harnesses, not by reading the diff.
validation.schema_validation: The Phase 4.1 validation run passed 15/15 manifest and catalog schema pairs. The run at the Phase 4.4 review passes 18/18 (Draft 2020-12 with format checking, jsonschema 4.26.0) on 2026-11-22 local: package 4.2 added the RegControl pair and package 4.3 the LoadShape pair, while package 4.4 populated the existing python_interface_comparison pair rather than adding one. The Phase 5.3 run passes 19/19 pairs, the symbol alias registry being the nineteenth, and each of four registered-registry malformations (unknown property, empty record ids, missing source ids, empty alias) fails validation.
validation.runtime: All 19 catalogued examples pass on the pinned stack (altdss 0.2.4, dss-python 0.15.7, backend 0.14.5, opendssdirect.py 0.9.4), and all three fixture runs pass against their revision 1 goldens (ieee13 snapshot: 16 buses, 38 elements, 2 total iterations; ieee13 daily: 24 steps; ieee34 snapshot: 37 buses, 117 elements, 25 total and 6 control iterations). The cross-interface comparison reports three pairs per fixture with zero out-of-tolerance differences and zero nonzero numeric deltas, and every interface reports the same engine build line, 0.14.5 revision 87d85c2. Scope limit: that result validates the API layer and not the numerics, because all three wrappers share that binary. The architect review re-ran the harnesses and the comparison at 2026-11-22 local and reproduced every recorded hash and the report byte-for-byte. The Phase 5.3 run reproduced 19/19 examples, three fixture runs and both `search_catalogs.py --check` sections at release v1.0.0.

known_gaps: No catalog file is empty. opendss_objects was populated by Phase 5.1 with 24 thin records — the 16 catalogued classes and the 8 deferred by decision 17 — carrying pointers and measured counts rather than property rows, and its schema rejects a record that restates properties. troubleshooting holds 16 confirmed records from Phase 4.5 and python_interface_comparison 13 accessor records from Phase 4.4. One catalog is deliberately outside the validated and searched corpus: references/lines/opendss_line_linecode_properties_legacy.json, retained for provenance and the repository's only holder of `Official-current` labels (63).

The generated altdss_python_api catalog covers object and collection classes and the AltDSS context. Non-element context interfaces, context batch proxies, and internal _str proxies are outside the catalog scope.

dss_capi.json covers Line, LineCode, LineGeometry, LineSpacing, WireData, CNData, TSData, Circuit creation, Vsource, Transformer, XfmrCode, Load, Capacitor, and Generator, including inherited fields used in these packages.
Transformer and XfmrCode coverage is limited to two and three windings. AutoTrans is deferred pending an owner scope decision.
The GrowthShape property catalog is deferred. LoadShape was catalogued in Phase 4 package 4.3; the Load package covers the Load element and its shape-assignment behavior only.
Property-level source_refs remain partial for Line/LineCode (E-3 deferred); new element packages require per-row citations.

Golden fixtures exist for both IEEE circuits at revision 1: snapshot on ieee13 and ieee34 and a 24-step daily profile on ieee13, all three reproduced byte-identically by the architect review. Residual gaps: no year-long QSTS run, no harmonic or unbalanced-fault study, and the daily profile covers one fixture only.
The beta package line (AltDSS-Python 0.3.0b2 and later) is documented as future compatibility only and not validated.
EPRI online pages do not state one OpenDSS version; version-sensitive claims need release-specific confirmation.
The legacy line catalog and builder are retained for provenance and are not active inputs.
CapControl is a deferred controller catalog. The Capacitor package covers the Capacitor element and the States control hook only.
The Capacitor element has no Spectrum property, unlike Load and Vsource.

The shared element schema now declares enum_type, reference_class, and dss_text_keyword. Optional array and write-path metadata cited in Capacitor architect finding O-1 still needs shared schema declarations.
GenDispatcher, CapControl, InvControl, PVSystem and Storage are deferred controller or element catalogs; the element packages cover element behavior and control hooks only.

Generator's built-in dispatch settings and separate GenDispatcher control are source-reviewed. The Model 3 snapshots use the default PVFactor; sensitivity to changing it is source-reviewed. Compiled models, dynamic studies, harmonics, and fuel consumption are outside runtime scope.

CapControl, GenDispatcher, GrowthShape, PVSystem, Storage and AutoTrans remain uncatalogued pending an owner scope decision (decision 17); RegControl was catalogued in Phase 4.2 and LoadShape in Phase 4.3.
next_actions: Phase 4 package 4.1 (fixture harness and snapshot goldens) is accepted by the owner (decision 16). The fixture pin and both revision 1 goldens are now fixed reference data: later packages may add goldens but must not change the fixture bytes or revision 1, and any change that moves a golden value requires a new revision with a recorded reason. E-1 stays closed by document, so no package change is required.
Phase 4 package 4.2 (RegControl catalog) is accepted by the owner (decision 18). Its one finding, F-1, is a rider on package 4.3: state that an out-of-range positive PTPhase reads back as 1.
Phase 4 package 4.3 (LoadShape catalog and the ieee13 daily profile) is accepted by the owner (decision 19). The daily golden is now reference data at revision 1.

Phase 4 package 4.4 (cross-interface comparison with opendssdirect.py 0.9.4) is accepted by the owner (decision 20); the architect review passed with no required corrections. The result validates the API layer only: all three interfaces wrap DSS C-API 0.14.5 and opendssdirect declares dss-python==0.15.7.

Phase 4 package 4.5 (exit) is accepted by the owner (decision 21), which closes the Phase 4 stop gate; both required corrections were verified applied at 0187ded: the exit checklist now carries the fixture-checksum gate (proved by a tampered-copy run that fails only the affected fixture and exits 1) and an executable class-coverage check that prints the eight fixture classes and exits 0, and row 5 records the QA/QC PASS. The gate is recorded as eight checks: the plan's six plus the design's fixture-checksum and class-coverage gates. Decision 17 defers the GrowthShape, CapControl, GenDispatcher, AutoTrans, PVSystem, Storage, InvControl and ExpControl catalogs.

Phase 5 (retrieval and release) is scoped by decision 22: `opendss_objects` is a thin index, not a second property catalog. Package 5.1 is issued with 24 records required — the 16 catalogued classes as pointers with measured counts, plus the 8 classes deferred by decision 17 with status deferred so a retrieval query lands on a truthful answer. Every count must be re-derivable by the architect from the file it names. Package 5.2 adds the retrieval tool and 5.3 the release record.

Repository state at Phase 4 close: `main` is the only branch locally and on the remote, in sync at the merge commit, and `wp/phase1` through `wp/phase4` were deleted after verification that each was an ancestor of the merge. Phase 5 work proceeds on `wp/phase5` and is merged to `main` at phase close.

Phase 5 package 5.1 (thin object index) is accepted by the owner (decision 23) after QA/QC and an architect review that re-derived every count: PASS, no required corrections. The index holds 24 records — the 16 catalogued classes and the 8 deferred ones — and every count in it was re-derived by the architect from the file it points at. Five EPRI pointers were fetched live and all resolve. Awaits owner acceptance; 5.2 (retrieval tool) is delivered and reviewed: PASS, no required corrections. search_catalogs.py answers symbol, concept, class, version and evidence queries over 926 addressable records with a citation, tag and access date per hit, and its --check mode re-derives the object index so a stale count exits 1 with the record and field named. The architect review ran every canonical query, corrupted three index fields in a scratch copy to prove `--check` exits 1 and names the record and field, and recorded that a corrupted `fixture_usage` entry is caught by the schema instead of `--check`. Package 5.3 (release record) is issued: charter step 7 satisfied by `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release/README.md` with the five named sections, and `references/symbol_aliases.json` behind its own schema so the `TapNumber` alias stops being a hard-coded branch.

Deferred class catalogs are settled (decision 17): LoadShape enters package 4.3 because the daily series cannot vary load without it, and GrowthShape, CapControl, GenDispatcher, AutoTrans, PVSystem, Storage, InvControl and ExpControl are deferred on scope grounds. Measured on the pinned stack before scoping: no pinned fixture uses any of them, and the circuits contain only load, linecode, line, transformer, regcontrol and capacitor. The deferral is not an evidence gap for CapControl or AutoTrans, which EPRI does document, so re-opening them needs only a reason to test them.

Phase 5 package 5.3 (release record) is issued under charter step 7 and is the last Phase 5 package. It requires five deliverables: `CHANGELOG.md` at the repository root with every date a `git log` supports; `docs/release/README.md` carrying package versions, source check date, validation levels, known gaps and supported tasks as five named sections, with the single `Unverified` record (`Line.epsrmedium`) named rather than rounded into a total, and every supported task naming a workflow page plus an example id or fixture run; `references/symbol_aliases.json` and its schema registered so the validation run goes 19/19, with `search_catalogs.py` reading the alias instead of branching on it and `--check` verifying each listed record exists and carries the canonical symbol; a `skill.md` whose phase paragraph is no longer stale, still under 90 lines; and a build audit mapping each charter release item to the section that satisfies it. The coder must not create a tag or move `schema_version` past `0.3.0-draft`: the version decision is the owner's and the tag is applied by the architect at acceptance. It also carried forward the 5.2 observation that `fixture_usage` accuracy is expressed only by the schema, not by `--check`. That package was delivered, reviewed with two findings (R-1 the alias registry undocumented in the retrieval workflow and package README, F-2 the `Official-current` scope clause), remediated and accepted as decision 25.

Release v1.0.0 is accepted and tagged (decision 25). Phase 5 is closed and every phase is complete. Standing work if the project continues: the eight classes deferred by decision 17 need an owner scope decision before they can be catalogued; the 63 `Official-current` labels in the legacy line catalog are excluded from validation and search by design and should not be cited as current evidence; `Line.epsrmedium` remains the one `Unverified` record and must stay out of generated calls to the pinned target; and the beta package line (AltDSS-Python 0.3.0b2+) is documented as future compatibility only and has never been validated.
